position: mid or end

senses.gloss: As a guess, without firm evidence.
examples: Some writers have *speculatively* linked the two events.
The report *speculatively* puts the final cost at $2 billion.
He talked *speculatively* about running for office someday.

position: mid or end

senses.gloss: Quickly; without delay.
examples: The problem was *speedily* resolved.
The judge wants the case handled *speedily*.
Volunteers worked *speedily* to fill the sandbags.

position: before its word — before adjectives and participles (*spiritually renewed*); also front

senses.gloss: In a way that concerns the soul, religion, or inner life.
examples: After the retreat, she felt *spiritually* renewed.
Many people are *spiritually* hungry but never go to church.
*Spiritually*, the trip changed his life.

position: end — or mid, before the verb

senses.gloss: With a wish to hurt or annoy someone.
examples: She *spitefully* deleted all his photos.
'Good luck with that,' he said *spitefully*.
The neighbor *spitefully* parked across our driveway.

position: end — or before a participle (*splendidly decorated*)

senses.gloss: Very well; in an impressive way.
examples: The kids behaved *splendidly* at the wedding.
Everything went *splendidly*.
The hall was *splendidly* decorated for the holidays.

position: mid or end

senses.gloss: Without planning, on a sudden impulse.
examples: The crowd *spontaneously* broke into applause.
We decided *spontaneously* to drive to the beach.

senses.gloss: By itself, without an outside cause.
examples: The pile of oily rags *spontaneously* caught fire.
In most cases the pain goes away *spontaneously*.

position: before its word — *spookily accurate*; end with verbs

senses.gloss: In a strange, slightly frightening way.
examples: Her prediction turned out to be *spookily* accurate.
The two sisters look *spookily* alike.
The wind howled *spookily* through the empty house.

position: before its word — almost always *spotlessly clean*

senses.gloss: Perfectly, with no dirt at all.
examples: The kitchen was *spotlessly* clean.
He keeps his car *spotlessly* clean.
The hotel rooms were *spotlessly* maintained.

position: end — right before *in* or *on* (*square in the eye*)
modifies: verbs of hitting, landing, and looking
form: flat — the same form as the adjective *square*
contrast: Informal; careful writing uses *squarely*. *Fair and square* is a fixed phrase meaning 'honestly, by the rules': *We won fair and square*.

senses.gloss: Directly and exactly.
examples: She looked me *square* in the eye and said no.
The ball hit him *square* in the face.
The dart landed *square* in the center of the board.

position: end — or before a phrase with *on*, *at*, *with* (*squarely on the table*)

senses.gloss: Directly, exactly, and fully.
examples: The blame lies *squarely* with the management.
The ball hit him *squarely* on the head.
The new law is aimed *squarely* at small businesses.

senses.gloss: Openly and honestly, without avoiding something.
examples: It's time we faced the problem *squarely*.
The senator refused to answer the question *squarely*.

position: before its word

senses.gloss: To an amazing, almost unbelievable degree.
examples: The house was *staggeringly* expensive.
It's a *staggeringly* beautiful place.
The cost of the war was *staggeringly* high.

position: before its word — only in *stark naked* and *stark raving mad*
form: flat — the same form as the adjective *stark*
contrast: Only in these two fixed phrases. Elsewhere *stark* is an adjective (*a stark contrast*, *stark reality*), and its adverb is *starkly*.

senses.gloss: Completely, in a couple of fixed phrases.
examples: The toddler ran out of the bathroom *stark* naked.
You'd have to be *stark* raving mad to swim out there in January.
The kids were running around the backyard *stark* naked.

position: before its word — *starkly different*; end with verbs

senses.gloss: In a sharp, clear, often harsh way.
examples: The two candidates have *starkly* different views on taxes.
The report *starkly* warns of a coming water shortage.
Her bright dress stood out *starkly* against the gray walls.

position: before its word

senses.gloss: To a surprising, even shocking, degree.
examples: She has *startlingly* blue eyes.
The results were *startlingly* similar.
Prices rose *startlingly* fast last year.

position: mid — or before its word (*staunchly conservative*)
modifies: verbs of supporting and opposing; adjectives of political views

senses.gloss: Firmly and loyally, without changing your position.
examples: Her family is *staunchly* conservative.
He *staunchly* defended his decision.
The union *staunchly* opposes the plan.

position: mid
modifies: verbs of refusing and denying; adjectives like *loyal*

senses.gloss: Firmly, without giving in or changing.
examples: She *steadfastly* refused to name her sources.
He remained *steadfastly* loyal to his friends.
The company has *steadfastly* denied any wrongdoing.

position: mid or end

senses.gloss: Gradually and continuously, without stopping.
examples: Prices have risen *steadily* over the past year.
The snow fell *steadily* all night.
Her health is *steadily* improving.

senses.gloss: Firmly and calmly, without shaking or looking away.
examples: He looked at her *steadily* and waited.
She spoke *steadily* despite her nerves.

position: end — or mid, before the verb

senses.gloss: Quietly and secretly, so as not to be noticed.
examples: The cat crept *stealthily* toward the bird.
He *stealthily* slipped out the back door.
They moved *stealthily* through the dark hallway.

position: before its word — *hot*, and informally *mad*
form: the -ing form of *steam*, used as a degree word

senses.gloss: Extremely; mostly in *steaming hot*.
examples: Be careful, the soup is *steaming* hot.
The waiter set down two *steaming* hot plates of pasta.
Dad was *steaming* mad when he saw the dent in the car.

position: end

senses.gloss: At a sharp angle; sharply, of a rise or fall.
examples: The road climbs *steeply* into the hills.
Home prices fell *steeply* after the crash.
The path drops *steeply* down to the river.

position: before its word — before adjectives (*stereotypically feminine*); also end

senses.gloss: In a way that matches a fixed, oversimplified idea of a group.
examples: Pink was once seen as a *stereotypically* feminine color.
He's a *stereotypically* grumpy New York cab driver.
In the movie, the villain is *stereotypically* portrayed as a foreigner.

position: end — or mid, before the verb

senses.gloss: In a serious, strict, disapproving way.
examples: 'Sit down,' the teacher said *sternly*.
The judge *sternly* warned the jury not to discuss the case.
She looked at him *sternly* over her glasses.

ru: до смерти, ужасно (*bored stiff* — до смерти скучно)
position: after its word — after *bored*, *scared*, *frozen*, *worried*
form: flat — the same form as the adjective *stiff*
contrast: Informal and only after these few words. Elsewhere *stiff* is an adjective (*a stiff neck*), and the manner adverb is *stiffly*.

senses.gloss: Extremely, after a few participles.
examples: I was bored *stiff* at that meeting.
The kids were scared *stiff* of the dog.
By the time we got home, we were frozen *stiff*.

position: end

senses.gloss: In a rigid way, without bending easily.
examples: He got up *stiffly* after the long flight.
The old man walked *stiffly* to the door.

senses.gloss: In a cold, formal, unfriendly way.
examples: 'I have nothing to say,' she replied *stiffly*.
They shook hands *stiffly* and sat down.

position: end — after *stand*, *sit*, *freeze*

senses.gloss: Completely without moving.
examples: The deer stood *stock-still* in the headlights.
We froze *stock-still* when we heard the noise.
The children sat *stock-still* as the magician raised his hands.

position: mid or end

senses.gloss: Calmly and without complaining, in spite of pain or trouble.
examples: She *stoically* endured months of treatment.
He listened *stoically* as the verdict was read.
The fans waited *stoically* in the freezing rain.

position: end

senses.gloss: Calmly and without showing any feeling.
examples: He stared *stolidly* ahead, saying nothing.
The guard stood *stolidly* at the gate.
She chewed her food *stolidly* while the others argued.

position: end

senses.gloss: Coldly, without any friendly feeling.
examples: She stared at him *stonily* and said nothing.
He listened *stonily* to their apologies.
The audience sat *stonily* through his jokes.

position: mid
modifies: verbs of defending, denying, and opposing

senses.gloss: Firmly and bravely, of defending or denying something.
examples: He *stoutly* denied taking the money.
Local residents *stoutly* opposed the new highway.
She *stoutly* defended her son's behavior.

position: end — or mid
contrast: More common in British English; Americans usually say *right away*, though *straightaway* is still met in American reading. Also written *straight away*.

senses.gloss: Immediately.
examples: I knew *straightaway* that something was wrong.
She called the police *straightaway*.
Can you start *straightaway*?

position: end

senses.gloss: In a direct, honest, or uncomplicated way.
examples: She answered the question *straightforwardly*.
The instructions are written *straightforwardly*, so anyone can follow them.
He told us *straightforwardly* that the project had failed.

position: end — or before its word (*strangely quiet*); front as a comment

senses.gloss: In an unusual or odd way.
examples: He's been acting *strangely* all week.
The house was *strangely* quiet.
She looked at me *strangely*.

senses.gloss: Surprisingly; a comment on a fact, often in *strangely enough*.
examples: *Strangely* enough, nobody noticed.
*Strangely*, I wasn't nervous at all.

position: before its word — before adjectives and participles (*strategically placed*); also end

senses.gloss: In a way that is planned to achieve a goal or gain an advantage.
examples: Cameras were *strategically* placed around the building.
The town is *strategically* important.
We need to think *strategically* about the next five years.

position: mid or end
modifies: verbs of objecting and denying; verbs of effort

senses.gloss: With great effort or force, especially in objecting or denying.
examples: The senator *strenuously* denied the charges.
Parents *strenuously* objected to the new schedule.
Avoid exercising *strenuously* for a week after surgery.

position: before its word — before participles (*strictly forbidden*); front in *strictly speaking*

senses.gloss: Firmly, so that rules must be obeyed; also exactly, in *strictly speaking*.
examples: Smoking is *strictly* forbidden inside the building.
The rules are *strictly* enforced.
*Strictly* speaking, a tomato is a fruit.

senses.gloss: Only; for no other purpose.
examples: This is *strictly* a business meeting.
The information is *strictly* for your eyes.

position: end — or mid, before the verb
modifies: verbs of speaking and arguing; adjectives of opinion

senses.gloss: In a loud, harsh, forceful way, especially in giving opinions.
examples: She *stridently* criticized the new law.
He argued *stridently* for lower taxes.
The group has become *stridently* opposed to any compromise.

position: before its word

senses.gloss: In a way that is very noticeable or impressive.
examples: She's a *strikingly* beautiful woman.
The two paintings are *strikingly* similar.
Crime rates dropped *strikingly* fast in the 1990s.

position: end — or before a participle (*stringently tested*)
modifies: verbs and participles of testing and controlling

senses.gloss: Very strictly, with tough rules or standards.
examples: New drugs are *stringently* tested before approval.
The rules are applied *stringently* to all applicants.
Air quality is *stringently* regulated in California.

position: mid or end — also before its word (*stubbornly high*)

senses.gloss: In a determined way that refuses to change or give up.
examples: He *stubbornly* refused to ask for directions.
Unemployment remains *stubbornly* high.
She held on *stubbornly* to her old ideas.

position: mid
contrast: Usually not about studying: *studiously avoided* means 'carefully, on purpose avoided'.

senses.gloss: Carefully and deliberately.
examples: She *studiously* avoided looking at him.
The report *studiously* ignores the real problem.
He *studiously* took notes during every lecture.

position: before its word

senses.gloss: Extremely, in a way that amazes you.
examples: The view from the top is *stunningly* beautiful.
The plan was *stunningly* simple.
The team played *stunningly* well.

position: before its word

senses.gloss: To an amazing degree.
examples: The owner of the team is *stupendously* rich.
The project turned out to be *stupendously* expensive.
The band played *stupendously* well that night.

position: end — or front and mid as a comment

senses.gloss: In a foolish or dazed way.
examples: She stared *stupidly* at the screen, unable to think.
He was grinning *stupidly* at his phone.

senses.gloss: Used to say that something you did was foolish.
examples: *Stupidly*, I left my wallet in the car.
I *stupidly* forgot to save the file.

position: before its word — mostly in *sturdily built*

senses.gloss: Strongly and solidly.
examples: The table is *sturdily* built.
He's a *sturdily* built man in his fifties.
The shelves are *sturdily* made of oak.

position: end — or before a participle (*stylishly dressed*)

senses.gloss: In a fashionable, attractive way.
examples: She's always *stylishly* dressed.
The apartment is *stylishly* decorated.
The film is *stylishly* shot but boring.

position: front or end — also before adjectives (*stylistically similar*)

senses.gloss: In terms of style.
examples: *Stylistically*, the two books are very different.
The songs are *stylistically* similar.
The essay is *stylistically* weak but full of good ideas.

position: mid or end

senses.gloss: Without being aware of it.
examples: Maybe you *subconsciously* wanted to fail.
We *subconsciously* copy the body language of people we like.
He was *subconsciously* looking for an excuse to leave.

position: end — or front as a viewpoint

senses.gloss: Based on personal feelings or opinions, not facts.
examples: Beauty is judged *subjectively*.
*Subjectively*, the pain felt much worse than it was.
The essays are graded somewhat *subjectively*.

position: before its word — *sublimely beautiful*, *sublimely unaware*; end with verbs

senses.gloss: Wonderfully; also completely, as in *sublimely unaware*.
examples: The music was *sublimely* beautiful.
He seemed *sublimely* unaware of the trouble he'd caused.
She played the second movement *sublimely*.

position: end

senses.gloss: In a way that obeys others without arguing.
examples: The dog rolled over *submissively*.
She lowered her eyes *submissively*.
He nodded *submissively* and did as he was told.

position: mid or end — also before its word (*substantially cheaper*)

senses.gloss: By a large amount; considerably.
examples: Costs have increased *substantially* this year.
The new model is *substantially* cheaper.
Our plans changed *substantially* after the merger.

senses.gloss: In the main points; essentially.
examples: The two versions are *substantially* the same.
The report is *substantially* correct.

position: mid or end — also before adjectives (*subtly different*)
form: -ly from *subtle*: the -le becomes -ly, and the b stays silent

senses.gloss: In a slight, clever, or hard-to-notice way.
examples: The two versions are *subtly* different.
She *subtly* changed the subject.
The room was *subtly* lit with candles.

position: mid or end

senses.gloss: In a way that achieves the result you wanted.
examples: The surgery was *successfully* completed.
She *successfully* ran her own business for twenty years.
The rocket launched *successfully* this morning.

position: before its word — before comparatives (*successively harder*); also mid
contrast: Not *successfully*: *successively* means 'one after another' (последовательно), *successfully* means 'with success' (успешно).

senses.gloss: One after another, in order.
examples: The tests become *successively* harder.
Each generation has been *successively* taller than the last.
The company was *successively* owned by three different families.

position: end

senses.gloss: Clearly and in very few words.
examples: She summed up the problem *succinctly*.
Please answer each question *succinctly*.
As one critic put it *succinctly*, 'Too long.'

position: before its word — before (*a*/*an* +) adjective + noun
modifies: an adjective together with its noun
contrast: *Such* goes before a noun phrase, *so* before an adjective alone: *such a nice day*, but *the day was so nice*. The article comes after it: *such a*, never *a such*. As a determiner (*such people*, *no such thing*) it is not an adverb.

senses.gloss: To so great a degree, before an adjective and its noun.
examples: It was *such* a beautiful day that we stayed outside.
They're *such* nice people.
I've never eaten *such* good pizza.

position: before its word

senses.gloss: Enough for a purpose.
examples: The patient has *sufficiently* recovered to go home.
The room wasn't *sufficiently* large for the party.
Make sure the chicken is *sufficiently* cooked.

position: end

senses.gloss: In a way that hints at something, especially something sexual.
examples: He winked at her *suggestively*.
She raised her eyebrows *suggestively*.
The ad was criticized for how *suggestively* the models were posed.

position: before its word — before adjectives and participles (*suitably dressed*)

senses.gloss: In the right way or to the right degree for the situation.
examples: Make sure you're *suitably* dressed for the interview.
Everyone was *suitably* impressed by the view.
The children were *suitably* rewarded for their hard work.

position: end

senses.gloss: In a silent, bad-tempered way, because you are annoyed.
examples: 'I don't want to go,' he said *sulkily*.
She sat *sulkily* in the corner all evening.
The teenager shuffled *sulkily* up to his room.

position: end

senses.gloss: In a gloomy, unfriendly way.
examples: He stared *sullenly* out the window.
The prisoners listened *sullenly* to the new rules.
She answered *sullenly* and went back to her phone.

position: before its word — before participles (*summarily fired*); also mid
modifies: verbs of firing, dismissing, and punishing
form: -ly from *summary* in its adjective sense 'quick and without formalities'
contrast: Not 'in summary'. To mean 'to sum up', say *in summary* or *in short*.

senses.gloss: Immediately and without the usual discussion or legal process.
examples: He was *summarily* fired after the incident.
The rebels *summarily* executed their prisoners.
The judge *summarily* dismissed the case.

position: before its word — before participles (*sumptuously decorated*); also end

senses.gloss: In a rich, expensive, impressive way.
examples: The hotel lobby is *sumptuously* decorated.
We dined *sumptuously* on lobster and champagne.
The book is *sumptuously* illustrated.

position: end — or before a participle (*superbly located*)

senses.gloss: Extremely well.
examples: The team played *superbly* in the second half.
The hotel is *superbly* located near the beach.
She sang *superbly*.

position: end — or before adjectives (*superficially similar*); front as a viewpoint

senses.gloss: Only on the surface; without looking deeply.
examples: The doctor only examined him *superficially*.
The book deals with the topic *superficially*.

senses.gloss: In appearance, but not in reality.
examples: The two cases are *superficially* similar.
*Superficially*, everything seemed fine.

position: before its word — *supernaturally strong*; also end

senses.gloss: In a way that seems beyond the laws of nature; unbelievably.
examples: He seemed *supernaturally* strong for a man his size.
In the story, the old house is *supernaturally* protected.
She has an almost *supernaturally* good memory for faces.

position: mid or end

senses.gloss: Because of a belief in luck or magic.
examples: He *superstitiously* wears the same socks to every game.
She knocked on wood *superstitiously*.
Many hotels *superstitiously* skip the thirteenth floor.

position: before its word

senses.gloss: Extremely; to the highest degree.
examples: She was *supremely* confident before the race.
It was a *supremely* important moment in his career.
The chef is *supremely* talented.

position: before its word — before participles (*surgically removed*); also end

senses.gloss: By means of a medical operation.
examples: The tumor was *surgically* removed.
The broken bone had to be *surgically* repaired.

senses.gloss: With great precision, touching only the intended target.
examples: The editor *surgically* cut three scenes without hurting the story.
The new rule *surgically* closes a single tax loophole.

position: mid or end

senses.gloss: Secretly, so that others do not notice.
examples: He *surreptitiously* checked his phone under the table.
She glanced *surreptitiously* at her watch.
The meeting was *surreptitiously* recorded.

position: end — or before its word (*suspiciously quiet*)

senses.gloss: Without trusting someone; with suspicion.
examples: The guard eyed us *suspiciously*.
'Why do you ask?' she said *suspiciously*.

senses.gloss: In a way that makes people suspect something is wrong.
examples: The kids are *suspiciously* quiet.
A man was acting *suspiciously* outside the bank.

position: end

senses.gloss: In a pleasant, kind, or gentle way.
examples: She smiled *sweetly* at the waiter.
The baby was sleeping *sweetly* in her crib.
The choir sang *sweetly*.

position: mid or end

senses.gloss: Quickly and without delay.
examples: The police acted *swiftly* to calm the crowd.
The river flows *swiftly* after heavy rain.
Prices rose *swiftly* after the announcement.

ru: как по маслу, без сучка без задоринки
position: end — almost always after *go*
contrast: Informal and a little old-fashioned. It has nothing to do with swimming.

senses.gloss: Very smoothly, without any problems.
senses.ru: как по маслу, без сучка без задоринки
examples: The party went *swimmingly*.
So far, everything is going *swimmingly*.
The two dogs got along *swimmingly*.

position: mid or end — or front as a viewpoint

senses.gloss: As a symbol, to show a meaning or idea.
examples: She *symbolically* handed him the keys to the office.
The ceremony was held *symbolically* on the Fourth of July.
*Symbolically*, the new bridge joins two divided communities.

position: end

senses.gloss: With both sides or halves exactly alike.
examples: The windows are arranged *symmetrically* on both sides of the door.
Plant the trees *symmetrically* along the path.
The garden was laid out *symmetrically*.

position: end
contrast: False friend: it is about sympathy (сочувствие), not about being *симпатичный* — that is *nice* or *good-looking*.

senses.gloss: With kindness and understanding for someone's problems.
examples: She listened *sympathetically* to his story.
The nurse smiled at me *sympathetically*.

senses.gloss: In a favorable way; with approval.
examples: The film portrays the rebels *sympathetically*.
The board looked *sympathetically* on her proposal.

position: end — mostly after *used*

senses.gloss: With the same meaning.
examples: The two terms are often used *synonymously*.
In this article, 'weather' and 'climate' are not used *synonymously*.
Many people use 'Holland' and 'the Netherlands' *synonymously*.

position: before its word — before participles (*synthetically produced*); also end

senses.gloss: By a chemical process, not naturally.
examples: The vitamin can be produced *synthetically*.
*Synthetically* made diamonds are much cheaper.
The fabric is *synthetically* dyed.

position: mid or end

senses.gloss: Using an organized method, step by step.
examples: The police *systematically* searched every house on the street.
Women were *systematically* excluded from the club.
We need to go through the data *systematically*.

position: mid

senses.gloss: Without saying so directly, but understood.
examples: By saying nothing, he *tacitly* agreed to the plan.
The government *tacitly* approved the deal.
It was *tacitly* understood that nobody would mention the divorce.

position: end — or mid, before the verb

senses.gloss: Carefully, so as not to upset or offend anyone.
examples: She *tactfully* changed the subject.
He *tactfully* pointed out the mistake.
The complaint needs to be handled *tactfully*.

position: front — as a viewpoint; also before adjectives and at the end

senses.gloss: In terms of the methods used to win a game, battle, or contest.
examples: *Tactically*, it was a brilliant move.
The coach changed the team *tactically* at halftime.
The retreat was *tactically* necessary.

position: end — or mid, before the verb

senses.gloss: Without fighting back or showing any spirit; in a weak, disappointing way.
examples: He *tamely* accepted the pay cut without a word.
The home team lost *tamely* in the second half.
After a great first hour, the movie ends *tamely*.

position: before its word — mostly *only tangentially related*; also end

senses.gloss: Only slightly or indirectly; not about the main point.
examples: The question is only *tangentially* related to the topic.
The book mentions the war only *tangentially*.
He was *tangentially* involved in the scandal.

position: end — or mid, before the verb

senses.gloss: In a real, noticeable way that can be seen or measured.
examples: Voters want to see their lives *tangibly* improve.
Crime has fallen *tangibly* since the program started.
The new policy has not *tangibly* changed anything yet.

position: before its word — most often *tantalizingly close*

senses.gloss: In a way that makes you want something you cannot quite have.
examples: The team came *tantalizingly* close to winning.
The smell of fresh bread drifted *tantalizingly* from the kitchen.
The finish line was *tantalizingly* near.

position: end — usually after *said*, *replied*

senses.gloss: In a sharp, slightly unkind way.
examples: 'I didn't ask for your opinion,' she said *tartly*.
He replied *tartly* that he had better things to do.
The editorial *tartly* noted that the mayor was on vacation during the flood.

position: before its word — before participles (*tastefully decorated*); also end

senses.gloss: In an attractive way that shows good judgment about style.
examples: The living room is *tastefully* decorated.
The scene was handled *tastefully*.
She was *tastefully* dressed in a simple black dress.

position: end — or before a participle (*tastelessly decorated*)

senses.gloss: In a way that shows bad taste or may offend people.
examples: The room was *tastelessly* decorated in gold and purple.
He joked *tastelessly* about the accident.
The ad *tastelessly* used photos from the disaster.

position: end — or before a participle (*tautly written*)

senses.gloss: Stretched tight, with no slack.
examples: The canvas was stretched *tautly* over the frame.
Her skin was pulled *tautly* over her cheekbones.

senses.gloss: In a tight, tense style with nothing extra, of a book or film.
examples: It's a *tautly* written thriller.
The film is *tautly* directed and never drags.

position: end — or mid, before the verb

senses.gloss: While crying or nearly crying.
examples: She *tearfully* thanked everyone who had helped.
The children said goodbye *tearfully*.
He *tearfully* admitted his mistake in court.

position: end

senses.gloss: In a playful way that makes fun of someone.
examples: 'Nice haircut,' he said *teasingly*.
She *teasingly* called him 'Professor.'
He poked her *teasingly* in the ribs.

position: before its word — before adjectives (*technologically advanced*); also front

senses.gloss: In terms of technology.
examples: Japan is one of the most *technologically* advanced countries.
*Technologically*, the car was years ahead of its time.
The plan is *technologically* possible but very expensive.

position: end — or before its word (*tediously long*)

senses.gloss: In a long, dull, boring way.
examples: The meeting dragged on *tediously* for three hours.
The movie is *tediously* long.
He explained the rules *tediously*, one by one.

position: front — as a comment; also mid or end

senses.gloss: In a way that reveals something important.
examples: *Tellingly*, he didn't deny the story.
The company, *tellingly*, had no comment on the report.
She wrote *tellingly* about her years in prison.

position: before its word — before adjectives (*temperamentally unsuited*); also front

senses.gloss: Because of a person's natural character.
examples: He was *temperamentally* unsuited to politics.
*Temperamentally*, the two brothers are complete opposites.
She's *temperamentally* calm, even under pressure.

position: end — or before its word (*temptingly close*)

senses.gloss: In a way that makes you want something.
examples: A plate of cookies sat *temptingly* on the table.
The beach is *temptingly* close to the hotel.
The shoes were *temptingly* priced at $20.

position: end

senses.gloss: Firmly and with determination, without letting go.
examples: She fought *tenaciously* for her patients.
The ivy clings *tenaciously* to the wall.
The old man held on *tenaciously* to his land.

position: end — or mid, before the verb

senses.gloss: Gently and with love.
examples: He kissed her *tenderly* on the forehead.
She *tenderly* wrapped the baby in a blanket.
The nurse *tenderly* cleaned the wound.

position: end — after verbs of growth and change

senses.gloss: By ten times.
examples: Sales have increased *tenfold* since 2020.
The town's population grew *tenfold* in a decade.
The value of the painting has risen almost *tenfold*.

position: end

senses.gloss: In a nervous, worried way.
examples: We waited *tensely* for the results.
The two men faced each other *tensely*.
She sat *tensely* on the edge of her chair.

position: mid or end

senses.gloss: As a plan that is not yet final.
examples: The meeting is *tentatively* scheduled for Friday.
They've *tentatively* agreed to sell the house.

senses.gloss: In a hesitant, uncertain way.
examples: She smiled *tentatively* at the new neighbors.
He *tentatively* raised his hand.

position: before its word — before participles (*tenuously connected*); also end

senses.gloss: Only weakly or slightly, of a link or hold.
examples: The two cases are only *tenuously* connected.
He's clinging *tenuously* to his lead in the polls.
The movie is *tenuously* based on a true story.

position: end — or mid, before the verb

senses.gloss: Without much interest or enthusiasm.
examples: Investors reacted *tepidly* to the news.
The audience applauded *tepidly* at the end.
Critics *tepidly* received the sequel.

position: before its word — mostly *terminally ill*

senses.gloss: With a disease that cannot be cured and will cause death.
examples: Her father is *terminally* ill with cancer.
The hospice cares for *terminally* ill patients.

senses.gloss: Hopelessly, as a joking exaggeration.
examples: The show is *terminally* boring.
My brother is *terminally* lazy.
